article.title: Hit by an 18-Wheeler
article.author: Tiqua Jackson
article.content: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. Best Truck Accident Lawyers in Pearland, TX: 6 Firms to Consider A crash with an 18-wheeler on Highway 288 or the Sam Houston Tollway can turn life upside down in seconds. Medical appointments, insurance calls and missed work pile up fast, and choosing a lawyer can feel like one more burden. Pearland sits just south of Houston, so most of the firms handling serious trucking cases for local residents are based in the city. This shortlist covers six Houston-area firms worth a consultation, what each one emphasizes and the questions that help you compare them. Key Takeaways Our first pick stands out for a clearly published case process, from free consultation and investigation through negotiation and court. Several firms on this list highlight board certification in Personal Injury Trial Law, a specialist credential from the Texas Board of Legal Specialization. Trucking cases depend on evidence such as driver logs and black-box data, so ask each firm how quickly it moves to preserve records. Nearly every firm works on contingency, but the percentage and the handling of case expenses vary, so get both in writing. Texas generally gives you two years from the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. How We Picked We reviewed each firm's truck accident practice pages, attorney biographies and published fee information in November 2026. We looked for five things: a dedicated commercial-truck practice, a described investigation process, named credentials, practical access for Pearland residents and clear fee terms. 1. The Morgan Legal Group, PLLC This Houston firm maintains a dedicated 18-wheeler accident practice and lays out exactly how it handles a case from the first call to a possible trial. For Pearland residents who want a firm that explains its process up front, The Morgan Legal Group, PLLC is a strong first consultation. Pros A six-stage process covering consultation, investigation, personalized strategy, communication, negotiation and court representation Investigation that includes gathering evidence, reviewing medical records and consulting with experts A stated priority on consistent, transparent communication and regular case updates A 100% free initial consultation Cons The fee percentage is set in the engagement agreement, so confirm it at the consultation The office is in downtown Houston at 440 Louisiana Street, Suite 910, a drive up Highway 288 from Pearland Fees: The firm describes contingency-based fees, meaning attorney fees come from a recovery. Ask how case expenses are handled before you sign. Best for: Pearland residents who want a clear picture of each stage of their claim and a firm that commits to keeping them informed. 2. Arnold & Itkin Arnold & Itkin is a Houston trial firm with a dedicated truck accident practice. The firm says it researches, investigates and develops each case as though it is headed to trial. Pros Trial-ready preparation from the start of a case A dedicated Houston truck accident practice page Free consultation and contingency-based attorney fees Houston-based, within easy reach of Pearland Cons As a large firm, it is worth asking which lawyer would handle your file No individual fee percentage is published Fees: Contingency-based. Request the percentage and expense terms in writing. Best for: Victims of catastrophic truck crashes who want a firm built around trial preparation. 3. Sutliff & Stout Sutliff & Stout is a Houston injury firm founded by Graham Sutliff and Hank Stout. Both founders are board certified in Personal Injury Trial Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization. Pros Two board-certified founding partners A dedicated Houston truck accident practice Describes working with experts and handling insurer communications Free case evaluation and no legal fees without a financial recovery Cons Trucking is one of several practice areas rather than an exclusive focus The office is on Post Oak Boulevard in Uptown Houston, farther from Pearland than downtown Fees: No legal fees without a recovery. Ask separately about case expenses. Best for: Readers who place a high value on specialist trial credentials. 4. Zehl & Associates Zehl & Associates is a Houston firm that advertises representation across Texas. Its truck accident page describes the specific records it seeks in commercial-vehicle cases. Pros Describes collecting driver logbooks, black-box data and electronic control module records Consults treating physicians and medical experts Free consultations and contingency-based fees Statewide representation Cons No individual fee percentage is published Confirm where consultations and meetings would take place Fees: Contingency-based. Ask how expert fees are funded and deducted. Best for: Readers who want a detailed conversation about vehicle and driver records. 5. Abraham Watkins Abraham Watkins is a long-established Houston firm with a downtown office. Its truck accident page describes a rapid-response investigation team. Pros A rapid-response team for early investigation Focus on preserving black-box data, driver logs and scene photographs Board-certified personal injury trial lawyers among its attorneys Contingency-based representation Cons Its stated trucking focus is severe injury and wrongful death, so ask early about less serious claims No individual fee percentage is published Fees: Contingency-based. Ask whether expenses are deducted before or after the attorney fee. Best for: Families dealing with catastrophic injuries or a wrongful death. 6. Terry Bryant Accident & Injury Law Terry Bryant opened his Houston firm in 1985. He is board certified in Personal Injury Trial Law and served 22 years as a municipal judge in Spring Valley Village. Pros A board-certified founder with experience on the bench A dedicated Houston truck accident practice page Free consultation Says the fee percentage is agreed in writing before work begins Cons The office is on the Katy Freeway in west Houston, the longest drive from Pearland on this list Ask which attorney would personally handle your case Fees: Contingency-based, with the percentage agreed in writing up front. Ask separately about expenses. Best for: Readers who value a long-established firm and a founder with judicial experience. Questions to Ask at Every Consultation Rule 1.04(d) of the Texas Disciplinary Rules of Professional Conduct requires contingency fee agreements to be in writing and to state how the fee is determined. Read the expense provisions as closely as the percentage. Bring the same questions to each meeting so the answers are easy to compare: Who will handle my case day to day? Which evidence will you request first, and how fast? Are expenses deducted before or after the attorney fee? What would I owe if there is no recovery? How often will I get updates, and from whom? For a broader look at how claims move from crash to settlement, see this guide to Texas personal injury cases . Conclusion Our first pick is the strongest starting point for Pearland residents who want a firm with a clearly explained process and a commitment to regular communication. Its free consultation makes it easy to learn how the firm would approach your crash before committing. The other five firms each bring something specific, from trial-first preparation and board-certified founders to detailed truck-evidence collection and judicial experience. Consider meeting with more than one, compare written fee terms side by side and move quickly, since trucking evidence can disappear in weeks. This article is general information, not legal advice. Check the proposed lawyer's Texas license and relevant trucking experience before you hire. FAQ How long do I have to file a truck accident lawsuit in Texas? Texas generally allows two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. Evidence such as driver logs and black-box data can be lost much sooner, so it helps to speak with a lawyer early. How much does a truck accident lawyer cost? Most truck accident lawyers work on contingency, taking a percentage of any recovery. Texas requires that agreement in writing, so compare the percentage and the treatment of expenses before signing. What if I was partly at fault for the crash? Texas uses a modified comparative fault rule. You can recover damages if you are 50% or less responsible, though your award is reduced by your share of fault. Do I need a lawyer based in Pearland? Not necessarily. Many experienced trucking lawyers serving Pearland are based in Houston, so focus on trucking experience, credentials and communication, then confirm how meetings would work. What evidence matters most in an 18-wheeler case? Driver logs, black-box and electronic control module data, maintenance records, scene photos and medical records are often central. A lawyer can send preservation requests to the trucking company quickly.
